structured_output.summary: Removed the duplicated keycap styling by reusing the existing panel classes. In src/ui/keycap-legend.ts, key() now gives each keycap the classes 'ui-panel ui-panel--cream ui-keycap', the same way hud.ts builds 'ui-panel ui-panel--mustard ui-hud-best'. In src/ui/components.css, I deleted the five declarations from .ui-keycap that .ui-panel and .ui-panel--cream already set (border, border-radius, box-shadow, background, color) and updated its comment. .ui-keycap--primary has the same specificity and comes later in the file, so the GAS key is still rally-red with a cream glyph. The legend sits outside .ui-hud, so the desktop rule `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-panel` (4px outline) doesn't reach the keycaps, and their computed style is unchanged. This is a duplication finding, so behaviour is meant to stay the same. The new guard test therefore passes both before and after the change. I checked that it does catch a regression: with the panel classes taken off the keycaps (the CSS already reduced), it fails. It renders the hud--first-lap stage at 1440×900 in Chromium and checks that the four cream keycaps compute the same border, radius, shadow, background and colour as the token variables (--outline-default, --color-ink, --radius-rect, --shadow-hud, --color-cream), and that GAS computes the rally-red/cream pair. pnpm typecheck passes and pnpm test passes (82 files, 612 tests). The 1440×900 first-lap screenshot shows the legend looking as it did before.
